what_it_does: Large storage systems (think cloud storage with millions of files) protect data against drive failures using a technique called erasure coding — mathematically spreading data across many drives so that even if some fail, the original data can be reconstructed. When a drive fails, 'repair' traffic (reading data from surviving drives to rebuild the lost pieces) competes with normal user traffic over the same shared network links, slowing down both. ChameleonEC breaks the repair job into many small tasks and dynamically assigns each task to network paths that currently have spare capacity, steering traffic away from links already busy with user requests. It also watches for 'straggler' nodes — drives or servers that are unexpectedly slow — and reroutes around them on the fly. The result is faster recovery with less interference to ongoing user activity.
